title: Matching object as the limit over all proper faces
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a category with finite limits [def-galois-finite-limits-colimits], let $K$ be a simplicial object of $\mathcal C$ with simplicial operators $K(\varphi)$ and face maps $d_i$ [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-object], and let $n\geq1$. Let $\mathcal I_n$ be the finite category whose objects are the injective order-preserving maps $\delta:[k]\to[n]$ with $0\leq k<n$, a morphism from $\delta':[k']\to[n]$ to $\delta:[k]\to[n]$ being an order-preserving map $\varepsilon:[k']\to[k]$ with $\delta\circ\varepsilon=\delta'$; let $P_n(K):\mathcal I_n^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathcal C$ be the diagram $\delta\mapsto K_k$ (for $\delta$ with source $[k]$), $\varepsilon\mapsto K(\varepsilon):K_k\to K_{k'}$. Let $\delta_i:[n-1]\to[n]$ be the increasing injection omitting $i$, and let $M_n(K)$, $\mathrm{pr}_i:M_n(K)\to K_{n-1}$ ($0\leq i\leq n$) and $\mu_n:K_n\to M_n(K)$ be the matching object, its projections and the matching morphism of [lem-weil-pbc-simplicial-matching-object]. Then: (1) for every object $W$ of $\mathcal C$, the map $(x_\delta)_\delta\mapsto(x_{\delta_0},\dots,x_{\delta_n})$ is a bijection, natural in $W$, from the families $(x_\delta:W\to K_k)_{\delta}$ indexed by the objects $\delta:[k]\to[n]$ of $\mathcal I_n$ with $K(\varepsilon)\circ x_\delta=x_{\delta\circ\varepsilon}$ for every morphism $\varepsilon$ of $\mathcal I_n$, onto the tuples $(x_0,\dots,x_n)$ of morphisms $x_i:W\to K_{n-1}$ with $d_{j-1}\circ x_i=d_i\circ x_j$ for all $0\leq i<j\leq n$; (2) for every object $\delta$ of $\mathcal I_n$ and every factorization $\delta=\delta_i\circ\varepsilon$ the morphism $\pi_\delta=K(\varepsilon)\circ\mathrm{pr}_i:M_n(K)\to K_k$ does not depend on the factorization, and $(M_n(K),(\pi_\delta)_\delta)$ is a limit cone of $P_n(K)$; (3) $\pi_\delta\circ\mu_n=K(\delta)$ for every object $\delta$ of $\mathcal I_n$, so $\mu_n$ is the unique morphism $K_n\to M_n(K)$ whose $\delta$-component is $K(\delta)$ for every $\delta$.

source.place: Lemma 0186 (lemma-formula-limit) and its proof, there for all maps $\alpha:[k]\to[n]$ with $k<n$; the same argument restricted to the injective $\alpha$ (the factorization $\alpha=\delta_i\circ\psi$ and $\alpha=\delta_{i,j}\circ\xi$ keeps $\psi$, $\xi$ injective)

proof.text: Objects of $\mathcal I_n$ factor through a face. Let $\delta:[k]\to[n]$ be an object of $\mathcal I_n$. Since $k<n$ and $\delta$ is injective, $\delta([k])$ has $k+1<n+1$ elements, so some $i\in[n]$ is not in the image of $\delta$. For every such $i$, [lem-weil-pbc-simplex-face-factorization] gives a unique order-preserving $\psi:[k]\to[n-1]$ with $\delta=\delta_i\circ\psi$, and $\psi$ is injective. Conversely a factorization $\delta=\delta_i\circ\psi$ forces $i\notin\delta([k])$. Since $\delta_i:[n-1]\to[n]$ is injective with $n-1<n$, it is an object of $\mathcal I_n$, and $\psi$ is a morphism $\delta\to\delta_i$ of $\mathcal I_n$. So the factorizations $\delta=\delta_i\circ\varepsilon$ in (2) are exactly the pairs $(i,\psi)$ with $i\notin\delta([k])$ and $\psi$ the unique factor, and there is at least one. (This is the restriction of 'Since $k\leq n$ the map $\alpha$ is not surjective. Hence we can write $\alpha=\delta^{n+1}_i\circ\psi$' to injective $\alpha$, the factor staying injective.)

The map of (1) lands in the tuples. Let $(x_\delta)_\delta$ be a family as in (1), on an object $W$, and put $x_i=x_{\delta_i}:W\to K_{n-1}$. For $n=1$ there is no condition on $(x_0,x_1)$ ([lem-weil-pbc-simplicial-matching-object] (2)). For $n\geq2$ and $0\leq i<j\leq n$, [lem-weil-pbc-simplex-face-face-identity] (in degree $n$) gives $\delta_i\circ\delta_{j-1}=\delta_j\circ\delta_i=:\delta_{i,j}:[n-2]\to[n]$, an injective map, hence an object of $\mathcal I_n$, and $\delta_{j-1}:\delta_{i,j}\to\delta_i$, $\delta_i:\delta_{i,j}\to\delta_j$ are morphisms of $\mathcal I_n$ (here $\delta_{j-1},\delta_i:[n-2]\to[n-1]$). With $d_m=K(\delta_m)$ [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-object] the compatibility of the family gives $d_{j-1}\circ x_i=K(\delta_{j-1})\circ x_{\delta_i}=x_{\delta_i\circ\delta_{j-1}}=x_{\delta_j\circ\delta_i}=K(\delta_i)\circ x_{\delta_j}=d_i\circ x_j$, as in the displayed computation of the proof of 0186.

The inverse map is well defined. Let $(x_0,\dots,x_n)$ be a tuple with $d_{j-1}\circ x_i=d_i\circ x_j$ for $i<j$. For an object $\delta$ of $\mathcal I_n$ choose a factorization $\delta=\delta_i\circ\psi$ (Step 1) and put $x_\delta=K(\psi)\circ x_i$. Independence of the choice: given $i$ the factor $\psi$ is unique (Step 1). Let $\delta=\delta_i\circ\psi=\delta_j\circ\phi$ be two factorizations with $i
eq j$, say $i<j$; then $i,j
otin\delta([k])$, so $\delta([k])$ has at most $n-1$ elements and $n\geq2$. Since $j-1\geq i$, $\delta_i(j-1)=j$; if $\psi(a)=j-1$ then $\delta(a)=j$, which is excluded, so $j-1
otin\psi([k])$ and [lem-weil-pbc-simplex-face-factorization] (for $[n-1]$) gives $\xi:[k]	o[n-2]$ with $\psi=\delta_{j-1}\circ\xi$. Then $\delta=\delta_i\circ\delta_{j-1}\circ\xi=\delta_j\circ(\delta_i\circ\xi)$ by [lem-weil-pbc-simplex-face-face-identity], and the uniqueness of the factor through $\delta_j$ ([lem-weil-pbc-simplex-face-factorization]) gives $\phi=\delta_i\circ\xi$. (This is the factorization $\alpha=\delta^{n+1}_{i,j}\circ\xi$ of the source, with $\xi$ injective because $\psi$ is.) Since $K$ is a contravariant functor [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-object], $K(\psi)\circ x_i=K(\xi)\circ K(\delta_{j-1})\circ x_i=K(\xi)\circ d_{j-1}\circ x_i=K(\xi)\circ d_i\circ x_j=K(\xi)\circ K(\delta_i)\circ x_j=K(\phi)\circ x_j$.

The family $(x_\delta)$ of Step 3 is compatible. Let $\varepsilon:\delta'\to\delta$ be a morphism of $\mathcal I_n$, so $\delta'=\delta\circ\varepsilon$. Choose $i\notin\delta([k])$ and $\delta=\delta_i\circ\phi$ (Step 1). Then $i\notin\delta'([k'])$ and $\delta'=\delta_i\circ(\phi\circ\varepsilon)$ is a factorization of $\delta'$, so by Step 3 (independence) $x_{\delta'}=K(\phi\circ\varepsilon)\circ x_i=K(\varepsilon)\circ K(\phi)\circ x_i=K(\varepsilon)\circ x_\delta$, using that $K$ is a contravariant functor [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-object]. (Last paragraph of the proof of 0186.)

Proof of (1): the two maps are mutually inverse and natural (the part the source leaves to the reader). Starting from a compatible family $(x_\delta)$ with $x_i=x_{\delta_i}$, the family built in Step 3 has $\delta$-component $K(\psi)\circ x_{\delta_i}$ for a factorization $\delta=\delta_i\circ\psi$; since $\psi:\delta\to\delta_i$ is a morphism of $\mathcal I_n$ (Step 1), compatibility gives $K(\psi)\circ x_{\delta_i}=x_{\delta_i\circ\psi}=x_\delta$. Starting from a tuple $(x_0,\dots,x_n)$, the $\delta_i$-component of the family of Step 3 may be computed with the factorization $\delta_i=\delta_i\circ\mathrm{id}_{[n-1]}$ (Step 3, independence), giving $K(\mathrm{id})\circ x_i=x_i$. Both maps commute with precomposition by any $g:W'\to W$, since they are given by postcomposition with fixed morphisms $K(\psi)$ or by selecting components; this is the naturality in $W$. Hence (1).

Proof of (2). By [lem-weil-pbc-simplicial-matching-object] (2) applied to $\mathrm{id}_{M_n(K)}$, the tuple $(\mathrm{pr}_0,\dots,\mathrm{pr}_n)$ satisfies $d_{j-1}\circ\mathrm{pr}_i=d_i\circ\mathrm{pr}_j$ for $i<j$. Applying Steps 3 and 4 with $W=M_n(K)$ and $x_i=\mathrm{pr}_i$: $\pi_\delta=K(\varepsilon)\circ\mathrm{pr}_i$ does not depend on the factorization $\delta=\delta_i\circ\varepsilon$, and $(\pi_\delta)_\delta$ is compatible, i.e. a cone on $P_n(K)$ with vertex $M_n(K)$. For an object $W$, the map $g\mapsto(\pi_\delta\circ g)_\delta$ from morphisms $W\to M_n(K)$ to cones on $P_n(K)$ with vertex $W$ (the compatible families of (1)) is the composite of the bijection $g\mapsto(\mathrm{pr}_i\circ g)_i$ of [lem-weil-pbc-simplicial-matching-object] (2) and the inverse bijection of (1) (Step 3 sends $(\mathrm{pr}_i\circ g)_i$ to $(K(\varepsilon)\circ\mathrm{pr}_i\circ g)_\delta=(\pi_\delta\circ g)_\delta$). So every cone on $P_n(K)$ factors through $(M_n(K),(\pi_\delta))$ by exactly one morphism, which is the definition of a limit cone of the finite diagram $P_n(K)$ [def-galois-finite-limits-colimits] ($\mathcal I_n$ is finite: finitely many injective maps $[k]\to[n]$, $k<n$, and finitely many maps between them). This is the statement 'the limit represents the functor of systems $(f_\alpha)$' of the proof of 0186, with the functor of the lemma represented by $M_n(K)$.

Proof of (3). For an object $\delta$ and a factorization $\delta=\delta_i\circ\varepsilon$, [lem-weil-pbc-simplicial-matching-object] (3) gives $\mathrm{pr}_i\circ\mu_n=d_i=K(\delta_i)$, so $\pi_\delta\circ\mu_n=K(\varepsilon)\circ K(\delta_i)=K(\delta_i\circ\varepsilon)=K(\delta)$ ($K$ contravariant, [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-object]). The family $(K(\delta))_\delta$ is a cone on $P_n(K)$ with vertex $K_n$ (for $\varepsilon:\delta'\to\delta$, $K(\varepsilon)\circ K(\delta)=K(\delta\circ\varepsilon)=K(\delta')$), so by the limit property of Step 6 there is exactly one morphism $K_n\to M_n(K)$ with $\delta$-components $K(\delta)$, and $\mu_n$ is it.

lean.statement: theorem matching_object_proper_faces_succ_succ {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] [HasFiniteLimits C] (K : SimplicialObject C) (n : ℕ) (c : Cone (matchingBoundaryIndex K n).multicospan) (hc : IsLimit c) (μ : K _⦋n + 2⦌ ⟶ c.pt) (hμ : ∀ i : Fin (n + 3), μ ≫ c.π.app (WalkingMulticospan.left i) = K.δ i) : (∃ E : ∀ W : C, ((Functor.const _).obj W ⟶ properFaceDiagram K (n + 2)) ≃ {x : Fin (n + 3) → (W ⟶ K _⦋n + 1⦌) // ∀ p : (matchingBoundaryShape n).R, x p.val.1 ≫ (matchingBoundaryIndex K n).fst p = x p.val.2 ≫ (matchingBoundaryIndex K n).snd p}, (∀ (W : C) (x : (Functor.const _).obj W ⟶ properFaceDiagram K (n + 2)) (i : Fin (n + 3)), (E W x).val i = x.app (op (properFace (n + 1) i))) ∧ (∀ (W W' : C) (f : W' ⟶ W) (x : (Functor.const _).obj W ⟶ properFaceDiagram K (n + 2)) (i : Fin (n + 3)), (E W' ((Functor.const _).map f ≫ x)).val i = f ≫ (E W x).val i)) ∧ (∃ π : (Functor.const _).obj c.pt ⟶ properFaceDiagram K (n + 2), Nonempty (IsLimit (Cone.mk c.pt π)) ∧ (∀ (a : ProperFaceCategory (n + 2)) (i : Fin (n + 3)) (ε : a.obj.left ⟶ ⦋n + 1⦌), ε ≫ SimplexCategory.δ i = a.obj.hom → π.app (op a) = c.π.app (WalkingMulticospan.left i) ≫ K.map ε.op) ∧ (∀ a : ProperFaceCategory (n + 2), μ ≫ π.app (op a) = K.map a.obj.hom.op) ∧ (∀ μ' : K _⦋n + 2⦌ ⟶ c.pt, (∀ a : ProperFaceCategory (n + 2), μ' ≫ π.app (op a) = K.map a.obj.hom.op) → μ' = μ))
lean.note: The two theorem statements cover degree one and every degree n+2. The definitions construct the index category and diagram explicitly introduced in this node. Matching objects and maps are arbitrary limiting boundary cones and their uniquely prescribed matching maps, using the dependency module, rather than a new choice of matching object.
